piece_type: Exhibit booth display and brochure at APA 2026 Annual Meeting (investigational drug)
category: Promotion of investigational / unapproved drug or use
letter_category_label: Preapproval promotion of investigational drug (safety/efficacy claims)
claim_text: “ALA-3000 Breaks Key Barriers in Ketamine Therapy for TRD” (brochure) | “Sustained-release profile for weeks without pronounced initial burst or dose dumping effect” (brochure) | “Potentially eliminates the mandatory ≥2-hour post-dose on-site monitoring required with ketamine therapies.” (brochure)
context: Investigational drug apparently studied only in Phase 1; booth placed near approved-product booths.
fda_rationale: Conclusory statements represent an investigational new drug as safe and effective for the use under investigation, violating 21 CFR 312.7(a).
suggested_check: For an unapproved/investigational product, does the piece make conclusory safety or effectiveness claims or otherwise promote the drug?

piece_type: Exhibit booth display and brochure at APA 2026 Annual Meeting (investigational drug)
letter_category_label: Misleading claims about safety (investigational drug; implied superiority)
claim_text: “No overall sedative, dissociative, psychosis-like side effects” (exhibit booth display) | “No sedation, dissociation, psychosis-like effects, or commonly ketamine-reported AEs (e.g., blood pressure elevation, urinary toxicity)” (brochure) | “No abuse signals” (brochure)
context: Ketamine is CIII with known risks of sedation, dissociation, respiratory depression, hemodynamic instability, abuse and misuse.
fda_rationale: Represents the investigational drug as safe and superior to approved ketamine therapies without adequate data.
suggested_check: Rule: flag absolute safety claims of the form 'No [adverse effect/abuse/side effects]' and 'no ... signals', especially for unapproved products.

piece_type: Exhibit booth display and brochure at APA 2026 Annual Meeting (investigational drug)
category: Promotion of investigational / unapproved drug or use
claim_text: The exhibit booth display did not include any information to indicate that ALA-3000 is an investigational new drug that has not been approved for commercial distribution in the United States.
context: Booth appeared in APA exhibit hall near booths for approved products.
fda_rationale: Absence of investigational status contributes to promotional representation of an unapproved drug.
suggested_check: Rule: for investigational products, require an explicit 'investigational / not approved by FDA' statement on every piece.

piece_type: HCP branded website webpages ("Efficacy and 2-year patient outcomes" and "Real VYEPTI experience")
category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
letter_category_label: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory)
claim_text: “During a 6-month chronic migraine pivotal study, 40% of patients treated with VYEPTI 300 mg were 100% migraine free for a month or more vs 22% with placebo” | “Give your patients the chance for 100% migraine freedom for a month or more” | “During the same period, 35% of patients treated with VYPETI 100 mg were 100% migraine free for a month or more vs 22% with placebo.”
context: Presented in conjunction with a prominent graphic of a woman standing in front of a large 100% image; "Post hoc analysis" appears only as a less prominent footnote, which FDA says does not mitigate the impression.
fda_rationale: Claims rest on a post hoc analysis of PROMISE-1/2 with no prespecified type 1 error control, so findings are exploratory; conclusory '100% migraine freedom' claims are unsupported and imply patients will be migraine-free.
suggested_check: Does the piece present results from post hoc / non-prespecified analyses as conclusive efficacy, with the post hoc caveat relegated to a footnote?
quote_check: verified (manual: letter splits the quote with a footnote)

piece_type: HCP branded website webpages ("Efficacy and 2-year patient outcomes" and "Real VYEPTI experience")
claim_text: “Reduce the impact of migraine for your patients” | “Patients on VYEPTI 300 mg experienced SUSTAINED REDUCTION in average headache pain severity over 2 years” | “>70% of patients on VYEPTI 300 mg reported their migraine symptoms were MUCH IMPROVED or VERY MUCH IMPROVED through 2 years” | “Increase potential for patient productivity and engagement in everyday life” | “>60% of patients on VYEPTI 300 mg reported IMPROVEMENT IN MIGRAINE ASSOCIATED DISABILITY through 2 years” | “Patients saw improvement in disability from first dose through 2 years, which resulted in more engagement at home, work, and in their social life”
context: Claims based on PREVAIL (open-label, single-arm) and a post hoc analysis; accompanied by graphs of MIDAS severity, PGIC, and MIDAS score over weeks 0-104.
fda_rationale: PRO endpoints (HIT-6, MIDAS, PGIC) had no alpha allocation and came from an open-label single-arm trial; instruments have validity/recall-bias limitations, so conclusory PRO/HRQoL claims are unsupported.
suggested_check: Are patient-reported outcome, disability, or quality-of-life benefit claims supported by a controlled, alpha-controlled endpoint using a fit-for-purpose instrument?

piece_type: HCP branded website webpages ("Efficacy and 2-year patient outcomes" and "Real VYEPTI experience")
claim_text: “~70% of patients reported increased satisfaction with their ability TO PLAN, BE PRODUCTIVE, AND PARTICIPATE in their daily lives” | “After starting VYEPTI, patients reported >2x THE AMOUNT OF MONTHLY GOOD DAYS” | “Of the 74 patients who stated they experience brain fog, 86% REPORTED IMPROVEMENT IN BRAIN FOG”
context: "Real VYEPTI experience" webpage; presented with attention-grabbing, colorful, bold graphics and charts with large font; based on REVIEW, an observational single-arm study.
fda_rationale: REVIEW had selection bias (required >=2 infusion cycles), no control arm, endpoints lacking validity/standard definitions, and long retrospective recall, so PRO claims are unsupported.
suggested_check: Does the piece cite real-world/observational single-arm data to claim patient-reported benefits (satisfaction, 'good days', 'brain fog') as if causally attributable to the drug?

piece_type: Consumer branded website webpage ('ATTR-CM')
category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
letter_category_label: Misleading presentation of study data (open-label extension)
claim_text: “Proven to help people with ATTR-CM live longer” | “People lived longer with continued treatment” | “The risk of death was lower over 3½ years with AMVUTTRA.*” with graphic “36% Lower Risk compared to placebo” | “80% Survival Rate for people taking AMVUTTRA at 3½ years compared to 72% for people taking placebo” | monotherapy tab: “35% Lower Risk compared to placebo”; “76% Survival Rate for people taking AMVUTTRA at 3½ years compared to 67% for people taking placebo”
context: 3.5-year mortality includes 6-month open-label extension after placebo patients switched; disclaimer 'This analysis was not included in the original study plan...' does not cure. FDA also received complaints about similar pieces.
fda_rationale: No concurrent control remained at 3.5 years; open-label extension cannot support definitive quantified mortality benefit.
suggested_check: Are quantified efficacy claims drawn from an open-label extension or period after control-arm crossover presented as controlled comparisons?

piece_type: DTC patient brochure (biosimilar)
category: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication facts
letter_category_label: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication information
claim_text: Presentations of the indications omit specific patient populations and administration in combination with other chemotherapies; page one and the header “What Is ALYMSYS® (bevacizumab-maly)?” on page two suggest monotherapy in all indications and list broad types of cancer with imagery; limitations of use not presented until page four.
context: Full indications only in ISI in small plain font after eye-catching graphics.
fda_rationale: Suggests general use across cancers or as single agent.
suggested_check: Rule: indication statements must include combination-therapy requirements, populations, and limitations of use at first mention.

piece_type: DTC patient brochure (biosimilar)
claim_text: Page four infusion presentation fails to disclose infusion-related reactions and suggests Alymsys “will be administered” regardless of IRR; page five: “Before receiving your ALYMSYS® treatment, tell your doctor if you: o Are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or plan to start a family in the future o Are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed …” without disclosing fetal harm, contraception, lactation, ovarian failure; omits “Withhold for at least 28 days prior to elective surgery” and arterial thromboembolic events.
context: ISI presents only W&P headings without material detail; 'see page 7 for ISI' statement does not mitigate.
fda_rationale: Omits material risk information and creates misleading impression of safety.
suggested_check: Rule: each W&P must include its key consequence/action (not just the heading); check pregnancy/lactation, IRR, and surgery-related instructions are present.

piece_type: DTC patient brochure (biosimilar)
claim_text: “It’s likely that you will experience side effects from your ALYMSYS® treatment. This is normal, and most side effects will resolve over time.”
context: Serious, sometimes fatal risks; 8%-22% discontinued for adverse reactions; cited ACS reference not product-specific. Risk not in severity order; complex medical terminology in consumer piece.
fda_rationale: Suggests all side effects resolve; minimizes serious risks.
suggested_check: Does reassuring language about side effects ('normal', 'will resolve') minimize serious or fatal risks in the label?

piece_type: DTC patient brochure (biosimilar)
letter_category_label: Unsubstantiated superiority / comparative claims (biosimilar vs reference)
claim_text: The totality of omissions and minimization misleadingly represents Alymsys as safer and more effective than the bevacizumab reference listed drug (AVASTIN® (bevacizumab)).
context: Biosimilar approval means no clinically meaningful differences from Avastin.
fda_rationale: Any suggestion that a biosimilar is safer/more effective than its reference product is misleading.
suggested_check: For biosimilars, does the piece imply safety/efficacy advantages over the reference product (explicitly or via omitted risks)?

piece_type: DTC broadcast TV ad ('January 2026 Pill Spot')
claim_text: VO: “The first and only FDA approved GLP-1 weight loss pill.” ON-SCREEN TEXT: “Only GLP-1 weight-loss pill” | VO: “Weight loss has never looked like this.” | VO: “The power of Wegovy, now in the palm of your hand.” | VO: “Weight loss with Wegovy isn’t a shortcut. It's a way forward.”
context: Efficacy from placebo-controlled trial only; no data showing superiority to other GLP-1s. Letter text is OCR (e.g., 'Meet Wegovy?® pill').
fda_rationale: Implies pill form offers superior efficacy/safety and outcomes not previously possible.
suggested_check: Does novelty of dosage form ('first', 'only', 'never looked like this') imply superior efficacy/safety without head-to-head data?

piece_type: DTC broadcast TV ad ('January 2026 Pill Spot')
claim_text: VO: “Now you can live lighter by losing weight.” ON-SCREEN TEXT: “LIVE LIGHTER™ by losing weight” | VO: “Live lighter by losing weight and keeping it off.” ON-SCREEN TEXT: “LIVE LIGHTER™ by losing weight and keeping it off”
fda_rationale: Implies additional weight loss vs other GLP-1s and emotional/psychological benefits not demonstrated.
suggested_check: Do slogans imply emotional, psychological, or life-direction benefits beyond the labeled clinical effect?

piece_type: DTC broadcast TV ad ('January 2026 Pill Spot')
category: Major statement not in dual modality (TV)
letter_category_label: Major statement not in dual modality (TV)
claim_text: The major statement includes presentations where there is information in the SUPERs that is not from the corresponding audio.
fda_rationale: Fails dual-modality requirement.
suggested_check: Rule: SUPER text during the major statement must match the audio.

piece_type: DTC TV ad
claim_text: “It’s my treatment, my way” with SUPER “VYVGART Hytrulo self-injection for treatment MY way” | “Vyvgart Hytrulo, for weekend-away Steve.” | “It’s travel ready, and can go where I go” with SUPER “VYVGART Hytrulo self-injection can go where I go.” | “Self-injection fits my plans” with SUPER “VYVGART Hytrulo A self-injection that can fit MY plans” (woman then tailgating at a stadium)
context: IFU: 30 minutes at room temperature on clean flat surface, supplies, hand washing, sharps disposal; small SUPER 'Travel ready in its original carton...' does not mitigate.
fda_rationale: Oversimplifies administration as easy while traveling or at outdoor events.
suggested_check: Do convenience/portability claims imply administration is simpler than the Instructions for Use require?

piece_type: DTC TV ad
claim_text: Major statement does not communicate: “Allergic reactions: …get emergency help right away if you have any of the following symptoms of an allergic reaction: rash, swelling of the face, lips, throat or tongue, shortness of breath, trouble breathing, low blood pressure, fainting” | “Infusion or injection-related reactions: …Tell your healthcare provider if you have any of the following symptoms...”
fda_rationale: Omits material W&P risk from the major statement.
suggested_check: Rule: each W&P in the PPI 'possible side effects' section must be represented in the TV major statement.

piece_type: DTC TV ad
claim_text: Zooming into food on a grill, tailgating with friends, a woman looking at a robotic arm, a man taking a selfie on a mountain path during the major statement.
fda_rationale: Attention-grabbing visuals interfere with comprehension.
suggested_check: Are visuals during the major statement engaging enough to compete with the risk audio?

piece_type: DTC broadcast TV ad
claim_text: “With a CLL diagnosis, there may be moments that seem unclear. But when it’s time for treatment, one thing is clear: Brukinsa.” | “See your future clearly again with Brukinsa. Ask your doctor about Brukinsa, the CLL treatment that keeps you in control.”
context: Man ascends mountain by gondola, overlooks landscape with family; adverse reactions most likely at start/dose change; regular HCP monitoring required.
fda_rationale: Implies patients can travel and maintain normal active lifestyle, downplaying serious side effects and monitoring.
suggested_check: Do 'in control'/lifestyle presentations downplay monitoring requirements or the timing of adverse reactions?

piece_type: DTC broadcast TV ad
category: Major statement not in dual modality (TV)
letter_category_label: Major statement not in dual modality (TV)
claim_text: Major statement includes presentations where verbatim key terms from audio do not appear in dual modality, and SUPERs contain information not from the audio.
fda_rationale: Fails dual modality.
suggested_check: Rule: compare audio and SUPER text of the major statement.

piece_type: DTC broadcast TV ad
claim_text: Major statement presented at emotional peak: man exits gondola holding hands with his wife, family laughing, hugs, complex handshakes and fist bumps, camera and map, photo with wife.
fda_rationale: Compelling visuals interfere with comprehension.
suggested_check: Does the major statement coincide with the ad's emotional climax?

company: Karuna Therapeutics, Inc., a Bristol Myers Squibb Co.
piece_type: DTC broadcast TV ad
claim_text: “Cobenfy showed overall improvement across a range of schizophrenia symptoms . . .” | on-screen “improvement ACROSS A RANGE OF SYMPTOMS” with overlapping circles “POSITIVE SYMPTOMS” and “NEGATIVE SYMPTOMS”
context: Opening on-screen symptom words include “Lack of emotion”, “Low motivation”, “Less social interaction”. Primary endpoint was PANSS total at Week 5; trials enrolled acute exacerbation patients, not designed to assess negative symptoms. SUPER does not mitigate.
fda_rationale: Implies improvement in both positive and negative symptoms when trials did not evaluate these as distinct groups.
suggested_check: Do claims or visuals attribute efficacy to symptom subdomains (e.g., negative symptoms) not separately established by the pivotal endpoints?

company: Karuna Therapeutics, Inc., a Bristol Myers Squibb Co.
piece_type: DTC broadcast TV ad
category: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication facts
claim_text: “If you still have symptoms, be bold and ask your healthcare provider about Cobenfy . . . .”
context: Placebo-controlled trials without active comparator; no treatment-refractory population enrolled.
fda_rationale: Suggests efficacy where other antipsychotics have failed, which has not been demonstrated.
suggested_check: Does the piece imply use after failure of other therapies ('still have symptoms', 'when others haven't worked') without supporting data?

company: Karuna Therapeutics, Inc., a Bristol Myers Squibb Co.
piece_type: DTC broadcast TV ad
claim_text: “Cobenfy is not an antipsychotic” with on-screen “not an antipsychotic”
context: SUPER: “A muscarinic agonist (xanomeline) and a muscarinic antagonist (trospium chloride)”.
fda_rationale: Cobenfy is considered an antipsychotic based on its indication and effects, not mechanism.
suggested_check: Rule: flag 'not a/an <drug class>' statements for verification against the product's therapeutic class.

company: Karuna Therapeutics, Inc., a Bristol Myers Squibb Co.
piece_type: DTC broadcast TV ad
claim_text: Compelling, attention-grabbing visuals (frequent camera angle changes showing Bryan skateboarding, greeting a friend, petting a dog, and setting up his DJ booth) during the major statement.
fda_rationale: Visuals interfere with comprehension of the major statement.
suggested_check: During the major statement, are visuals active/attention-grabbing (scene cuts, activities) such that they compete with risk comprehension?

piece_type: DTC TV ad (“A Game 60 TV Ad Pool Out 2025”)
claim_text: “Playdate? You bring your A-game;” | “Ready to score? You bring your A-game;” | “Bring your A-game to your sexual wellness.” | “You bring your A-game to everything you do. Ask your doctor about APRETUDE.”
context: Scenes of sexually suggestive behavior throughout; PI W&P says Apretude is used as part of a comprehensive prevention strategy including safer sex practices and condoms. Ad includes “APRETUDE does not prevent other sexually transmitted infections. Practice safer sex to reduce your risk.”
fda_rationale: Misleadingly suggests Apretude provides a sense of sexual freedom without the need to practice safer sex to reduce STI risk; the disclaimer does not mitigate the overall impression.
suggested_check: Pairwise judge: does the net impression of copy+visuals undercut a labeled safety behavior (e.g., safer sex/condom use) even if a disclaimer is present?

piece_type: DTC TV ad (“A Game 60 TV Ad Pool Out 2025”)
claim_text: frequent scene changes and attention-grabbing visuals (e.g., the sexually suggestive behaviors described above) during the presentation of the major statement
context: DTC TV major statement.
fda_rationale: Interferes with comprehension of the major statement.
suggested_check: Storyboard check: count scene cuts during major statement; judge whether visuals compete with risk audio.

piece_type: HCP branded website “Efficacy Data” webpage (US-FYA-2300007)
category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
claim_text: “DISEASE CONTROL RATE 71% of patients with a confirmed response or with SD of ≥12 weeks’ duration (95% Cl: 52%, 85.8%)” | bar showing 7% CR, 32% PR, 52% SD, 10% PD | waterfall plot “TARGET LESION CHANGES AT STUDY-END ANALYSIS (N=31)”
context: Approval based on ORR (CR+PR) and DoR in single-arm AMPECT. Disclaimers: “Disease control rate was a post hoc exploratory endpoint and was not prespecified...” and “…SD and PD could be due to the natural course of the disease and not due to treatment”.
fda_rationale: Single-arm trial cannot attribute SD (alone or within DCR) to the drug; DCR is unsupported; disclaimers do not cure.
suggested_check: Rule: in single-arm-trial products, flag 'stable disease' or 'disease control rate' claims; disclaimers do not count as a fix.

piece_type: HCP branded website “Efficacy Data” webpage (US-FYA-2300007)
category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
claim_text: “FYARRO goes the distance for patients with PEComa” | “MEDIAN PFS” “~1 YEAR (10.6 months; 95% CI: 5.5, 41.2 months)” | “MEDIAN OS” “>4 YEARS (53.1 months; 95% CI: 22.2 months to not reached)”
context: Kaplan-Meier graphs from single-arm AMPECT; footnote: “Survival data should be interpreted with caution given the single-arm study design.”
fda_rationale: Time-to-event endpoints from a single-arm trial are uninterpretable; tagline furthers implied survival benefit.
suggested_check: Rule: flag PFS/OS/median-survival claims when the source trial is single-arm (pair with label 'Clinical Studies' design).

piece_type: HCP branded website “Efficacy and Safety” webpage (ANK-00079-US-v4.0)
category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
claim_text: “% of Responders Who Were Cystectomy Free At 36 Months o 84%” | “Disease-Specific Overall Survival at 36 Months o 99%”
context: Approval based on CR and DoR in single-arm QUILT-3.032; Bad Ad complaint also received.
fda_rationale: Cystectomy avoidance and DSS are time-to-event endpoints; uninterpretable without a comparator.
suggested_check: Rule: flag PFS/OS/survival/time-to-event claims (incl. cystectomy-free, DSS) when the source trial is single-arm; disclaimers do not count as a fix.

piece_type: HCP professional newsletter “Science Behind Jeuveau” (US-JUV-2500066)
claim_text: “MANUFACTURING MATTERS-NOT ALL TOXINS ARE CREATED EQUAL” | “ENSURE PATIENTS GET THE FULL BENEFITS OF TREATMENT” | “Consistency and efficacy starts with manufacturing. Trust vacuum-dried Jeuveau®, a 900 kDa BoNT/A that utilizes the full complex with active accessory protein for full efficacy.” | “NAPs play an active role in BoNT/A [botulinum neurotoxin type A] activity…” | “BoNT/A with NAPs effectively reduce glabellar strain vs non-complexed formulation”
context: Multiple FDA-approved botulinum toxins for glabellar lines; no head-to-head studies; cited review article only theorizes.
fda_rationale: Suggests manufacturing/formulation gives benefits over other toxins when not demonstrated.
suggested_check: Judge: manufacturing/formulation/molecular-weight claims that imply class-comparative clinical advantage without head-to-head data.

piece_type: HCP professional newsletter “Science Behind Jeuveau” (US-JUV-2500066)
claim_text: “The field effect of the 900 kDa molecule may contribute to the precision profile, supporting the theory larger structures may diffuse less” | “Avoids crystal formation, helping maintain integrity of the toxin, including accessory proteins, for efficacy with less risk of antibody formation.” | “In clinical studies, vacuum-dried toxin formulations produced no antibodies after exposure.”
context: BOXED WARNING on distant spread of toxin effect; PI Immunogenicity section: potential for immunogenicity, cross-study antibody comparisons may be misleading.
fda_rationale: Minimizes distant spread risk and immunogenicity; references don't support.
suggested_check: Judge: claims like 'diffuse less' / 'no antibodies' that soften a boxed warning or PI immunogenicity statement.

piece_type: HCP sales aid “CCA CVA Update Print 8.5x11” (MAT-PEM-00577-v2)
category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
claim_text: “82% DCR (95% CI, 74-89)” | “DCR was defined as CR+PR+SD” | “82.4% DCR (95% CI, 74-89)”
context: Pages 8 and 10 (“FIGHT-202: ADDITIONAL ENDPOINTS”, “4-YEAR FOLLOW-UP ANALYSIS”); approval on ORR/DOR in single-arm FIGHT-202; disclaimers present. Complaints also received.
fda_rationale: SD/DCR not attributable to drug in single-arm trial; disclaimers do not cure.
suggested_check: Rule: in single-arm-trial products, flag stable disease / DCR / waterfall plots including SD; disclaimers do not count as a fix.

piece_type: HCP sales aid “CCA CVA Update Print 8.5x11” (MAT-PEM-00577-v2)
category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
claim_text: “Median PFS=6.9 months (95% CI, 6.2-9.6)” | “Median OS = 21.1 months (95% CI, 14.8-NE)” | “Median PFS = 7.0 months (95% CI, 6.1-10.5)” | “Median OS = 17.5 months (95% CI, 14.4-22.9)”
context: Kaplan-Meier graphs from single-arm FIGHT-202 incl. 4-year follow-up.
fda_rationale: PFS/OS from single-arm trial are uninterpretable.
suggested_check: Rule: flag PFS/OS/survival/time-to-event claims (incl. cystectomy-free, DSS) when the source trial is single-arm; disclaimers do not count as a fix.

piece_type: DTC TV ad “2025 CALQUENCE DTC Commercial - Major Statement Update” (US-99628)
claim_text: “When you’re ready to begin treatment… for chronic lymphocytic leukemia, CALQUENCE helps you do the fighting.” | “And you can do the exploring.” | “You can do the splashing…” | “…the sightseeing…” | “…and the playing.”
context: Images: man on cliff, woman splashing with grandson, couple sightseeing, man playing with dog. Patients require regular HCP monitoring.
fda_rationale: Suggests patients can maintain a normal, active lifestyle on treatment, downplaying serious side effects and monitoring requirements.
suggested_check: Judge: 'you do the living' lifestyle framing for oncology drugs with significant AEs/monitoring; pairwise vs. version acknowledging monitoring.

piece_type: DTC TV ad “2025 CALQUENCE DTC Commercial - Major Statement Update” (US-99628)
claim_text: [Visual] a man playing with a dog, a woman splashing in the swimming pool, and multiple background scene changes while a couple goes sightseeing — during the major statement
context: DTC TV major statement.
fda_rationale: Interferes with comprehension of the major statement.
suggested_check: Storyboard check: flag attention-grabbing visuals and frequent scene changes during major statement audio.

piece_type: DTC TV ad “TV 0:60 STORYBOARD: FEEL/SEE BASKETBALL” (3500-US-2500152)
claim_text: “Back to the game I love.” | “It’s great to be able to keep up with the guys again.” | “With CAMZYOS my symptoms have improved and I can be more active now.” | “It’s a difference I can feel…” | “… and they can see.” | “And she can too.” | “It’s great to be playing again.”

suggested_check: Judge: depicted activity level vs. responder rate in PI; flag implication that 'all patients' achieve it.

piece_type: DTC TV ad “TV 0:60 STORYBOARD: FEEL/SEE BASKETBALL” (3500-US-2500152)

piece_type: DTC TV ad “TV 0:60 STORYBOARD: FEEL/SEE BASKETBALL” (3500-US-2500152)

category: Major statement not in dual modality (TV)
letter_category_label: Major statement not in dual modality / incomplete major statement (TV)
claim_text: [Omission/Format] hypersensitivity information included only in the SUPERs; audio omits telling HCP or getting emergency help for allergic reaction symptoms (per Patient Package Insert); SUPERs and audio not verbatim/key-term matched

claim_text: “IN THE FRESCO-2 STUDY FRUZAQLA HELPED PRESERVE CERTAIN QUALITY OF LIFE MEASURES” | “A quality of life survey taken as part of the study showed more than 70% of people living with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) taking FRUZAQLA + BSC reported their symptoms staying the same or taking longer to get worse compared with people taking placebo + BSC.” | “Symptoms that took longer to get worse with FRUZAQLA + BSC vs placebo + BSC: o Emotional health o Social well-being o Tiredness (fatigue) o Nausea/vomiting o Trouble sleeping (insomnia)”
context: FRESCO-2 QLQ-C30/EQ-5D-5L secondary endpoints with no alpha allocation; attrition (esp. placebo); 7-day recall aligned to off-treatment days; confounding; time-to-deterioration ignores discontinuers. Disclaimer present.

category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
letter_category_label: Misleading presentation of study data (exploratory endpoint)
claim_text: SUPER: “Premenopausal women taking KISQALI with an NSAI and goserelin lived for 58.7 months vs 47.7 months on an NSAI and goserelin alone.” | VO: “. . .Then I learned about KISQALI. . .a pill that stops cancer from growing. . .and can help me live longer.”
context: PI final OS (MONALEESA-7): median not reached vs 40.7 months, HR 0.699. SUPER uses 54-month extended exploratory, non-prespecified analysis.
fda_rationale: Exploratory OS medians without context/limitations or full KM curve are misleading.

piece_type: HCP branded website “Efficacy Results” webpage (FUTI-PM-US-0024 v2)
category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
claim_text: “Median [PFS], 9.0 mo (95% CI: 6.9, 13.1)” | “Median [OS], 21.7 mo (95% CI: 14.5, Not Reached)” | “At a nonprespecified follow-up analysis conducted 8 months after the primary analysis ... efficacy in the overall study population was maintained with: ... “median PFS of 8.9 months” ... “median OS of 20.0 months”
context: Kaplan-Meier graphs from single-arm FOENIX-CCA2; disclaimers that single-arm time-to-event results may not be interpretable and extended follow-up data are descriptive.
fda_rationale: Single-arm design cannot establish PFS/OS effects; results uninterpretable; disclaimers do not cure.
suggested_check: Rule: flag PFS/OS/median-survival claims when the source trial is single-arm; disclaimers do not count as a fix.

piece_type: HCP branded website “Efficacy Results” webpage (FUTI-PM-US-0024 v2)
category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
claim_text: “Disease control rate (DCR) (n=103)” | “83% DCR (95% CI: 74, 89)” (pie chart) | “...efficacy in the overall study population was maintained with … DCR of 82.5%.”
context: DCR defined as CR + PR + SD; approval based on ORR (CR+PR) and DoR. Disclaimer: “FOENIX-CCA2 was a single arm study. In this setting, the DCR results may reflect the natural history...”
fda_rationale: SD in a single-arm trial is not attributable to the drug; DCR composite unsupported.
suggested_check: Rule: in single-arm-trial products, flag 'stable disease' or 'disease control rate' claims.

company: Otsuka Pharmaceutical Development and Commercialization, Inc
piece_type: DTC TV ad and DTC desktop display banner
letter_heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
claim_text: “When added to an antidepressant, REXULTI was proven to reduce depression symptoms 62% more than the antidepressant alone.” (Voiceover, frames 8-9) | “When added to an antidepressant, Rexulti was proven to provide a 62% greater reduction in depression symptoms” (Frame 3) | “When added to an antidepressant, Rexulti was proven to provide a 62% greater reduction in depression symptoms vs. the antidepressant alone.” (Frame 4)
context: Placebo-subtracted MADRS difference -3.2 from baseline 27 = 11.9% (Study 1); 4.8%/7.4% in Study 2; 'Individual results may vary' does not mitigate.
fda_rationale: Relative difference of change scores presented as a 62% symptom reduction greatly overstates benefit.
suggested_check: Rule: flag '% more/greater reduction' claims derived from ratios of change scores; recompute as placebo-subtracted difference relative to baseline.

piece_type: DTC video (sponsored TV segment) and HCP efficacy webpage
claim_text: “I've been using DUOBRII for 2 years, it works into my routine. I have cleared my plaque psoriasis on my elbows. I didn’t have flaky skin, it wasn’t sore, it wasn’t red.”
context: Female patient of childbearing age shown with two young children; video omits pregnancy test within 2 weeks, initiation during menses, and contraception; also omits photosensitivity (patient shown outdoors with exposed arms) and ophthalmic adverse reactions.
fda_rationale: Omits material facts about embryofetal risk mitigation, photosensitivity, and ophthalmic risks; suggests use without precautions.
suggested_check: Rule: each W&P (incl. required actions such as pregnancy testing, contraception, sun protection) must appear in the piece.

The creams I was prescribed were thick, and greasy, and they had an odor and they did not work for me.” | “When I first started using DUOBRII, I noticed how light and non-greasy it was. Within days, I started to see results.”

piece_type: DTC video (sponsored TV segment) and HCP efficacy webpage
category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
letter_category_label: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory)
letter_heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
claim_text: “Demonstrated synergy: superior efficacy vs the aggregated results of two monotherapies” | “More patients experienced treatment success with DUOBRII Lotion than the aggregated success rates of both monotherapies” | “DUOBRII Lotion exceeded the clinical definition of synergy by 31.7% at 8 weeks” | bar graph “Treatment success at 8 weeks with the effect of the vehicle removed.” (42.8% vs 32.5%)
context: Post hoc analysis of a small phase 2 trial; vehicle effect removed; actual absolute difference 0.6% (52.5% vs 51.9%). 'Post hoc analysis of a phase 2 clinical trial' statement does not mitigate.
fda_rationale: Exploratory post hoc data cannot support 'demonstrated synergy'/'superior efficacy'; vehicle subtraction inflates difference.
suggested_check: Do claims of synergy/superiority rely on post hoc analyses or manipulated baselines (e.g., vehicle subtraction) rather than prespecified endpoints?

piece_type: Professional 'Doctor Info' letter (HCP print piece)
category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
letter_category_label: Misleading presentation of study data (cross-study combination)
letter_heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
claim_text: “TOTAL* LDL-C REDUCTIONS o Roszet 10 mg/10 mg 64% o Roszet 20 mg/10 mg 66% o Roszet 40 mg/10 mg 72%” | “Roszet 5 mg/10 mg total LDL-C reduction is 59%.”
context: Asterisk note: '(1-52%)*(1-25%) = 36%' combining rosuvastatin monotherapy study with separate ezetimibe add-on study (different statins, populations, durations).
fda_rationale: Calculated by combining two unrelated studies; no scientific basis.
suggested_check: Are efficacy numbers derived by mathematically combining separate studies rather than from a study of the product itself?

piece_type: Professional 'Doctor Info' letter (HCP print piece)
category: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory / single-arm)
letter_category_label: Misleading presentation of study data (mITT/LOCF, secondary endpoints, timing)
letter_heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
claim_text: “Patients Can Get Below 70 mg/dL with One Pill Daily” | “Mean LDL-C Reductions Achieved in Clinical Trials” o “GRAVITY Study Baseline LDL-C 163 mg/dl Final LDL-C 65 mg/dl after 12 weeks (Dose: rosuvastatin/ezetimibe 10 mg/10 mg)” ... o “EXPLORER Study Baseline LDL-C 189 mg/dl Final LDL-C 57 mg/dl after 6 weeks (Dose: rosuvastatin/ezetimibe 40 mg/10 mg)”
context: mITT + LOCF bias; <70 mg/dL was one of many secondary endpoints without multiplicity control; GRAVITY week 12 = 6 weeks monotherapy + 6 weeks combination.
fda_rationale: Study limitations preclude quantitative conclusions; mischaracterizes treatment duration.
suggested_check: Are cited study results based on uncontrolled secondary endpoints, biased analysis populations, or mischaracterized treatment durations?
